record.name: Evacuation
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Evacuation: extract map-placed Civilians or enemy HVTs using Extraction Consoles, with two Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, score 1 Objective Point for each of the four Civilians successfully Extracted using an Extraction Console (up to four).
At game end, score 1 Objective Point for each opposing HVT successfully Extracted using an Extraction Console (up to two).
Each player has two Classified Objectives, worth 2 Objective Points each when completed (up to four), as specified explicitly in the English publication.

rules.name: Forces and Deployment
paragraphs: Players deploy at opposite table edges. Both Deployment Zones are [[distance:8:inch]] deep in 150-point games and [[distance:12:inch]] deep in 200–400-point games. Both languages show these dimensions on their published maps.
Troopers cannot deploy in Silhouette contact with a Civilian. Civilians and Extraction Consoles occupy fixed positions on the mission map; HVTs follow their normal player-selected deployment rules.

rules.name: Civilians
paragraphs: Four Civilians begin at the positions indicated on each game-size map. Each must be on an accessible point of the table, not on top of or inside scenery or buildings; terrain placement must allow this.

Use suitable civilian/HVT Models or Player A/B Tokens as the source permits. The source does not assign a fixed physical base diameter to the Civilian figures or Tokens, so map symbols indicate center positions only.
Civilians may be CivEvaced under the applicable CivEvac rules. Extraction is a separate successful Scenario Skill, not automatic from being CivEvaced.

rules.name: Multiple HVTs
paragraphs: Each player deploys two HVTs under the normal HVT deployment rules. The opponent's HVTs are eligible for Extraction and score 1 Objective Point each when successfully Extracted.
HVT locations are not fixed by the printed map. The four printed blue markers represent Civilians, not player-deployed HVTs.

rules.name: Extraction Consoles
paragraphs: Two Extraction Consoles begin on the table centerline at the printed positions. Each is a Console A Token or a scenery piece of the same diameter as that Token.
The Consoles are shared extraction points; activating a Console does not itself award points or establish exclusive ownership.

rules.name: Activate Extraction Console

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Extraction Console and CivEvacing a Civilian or enemy HVT may declare this Skill.
effects: Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts may be repeated.
On success, select one currently CivEvaced Civilian or enemy HVT, mark it Extracted, and remove it from the table.
restrictions: The English source prohibits this Skill during the first Game Round.
clarifications: The Spanish text uses 'primer Turno de Juego' for the opening restriction and explicitly permits re-Activating a Console activated by the opponent; the English source is silent on that latter point.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Extraction Console and CivEvacing at least one Civilian or enemy HVT may declare this Skill.
The English publication prohibits this Skill in the first Game Round. The Spanish publication instead uses 'primer Turno de Juego'; the different timing term is retained as a source issue.

Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. If it fails, another attempt can be made by spending another Short Skill. On success, choose one of the Civilians or enemy HVTs currently CivEvaced by that Specialist Troop, mark it Extracted and remove it from the table.

The Spanish source expressly states that a Console may be Activated after the opponent has Activated it; the English text is silent. Extraction is per successful action, not permanent Console Control.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform mission tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: If a Specialist Troop fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, its next consecutive Order using the same Skill and target receives +3 to WIP. The third and subsequent consecutive Orders receive +3 and +1SD. These MODs are cumulative with other applicable Scenario MODs.

The sequence resets on a successful Roll, using a different Skill or target, an interruption, or an Order spent on another Trooper. Only one sequence per Trooper and Scenario-labelled Skill applies at once.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 55 explicitly gives 2 Objective Points per Classified Objective for two Objectives. ES p. 50 instead states two Classified Objectives and '2 Puntos de Objetivo' without 'each'. Preserve this language-scope ambiguity; follow the explicit English scoring.

ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 57 prohibits Activate Extraction Console in the first Game Round; ES p. 52 uses 'primer Turno de Juego' (first Game Turn), not the usual Spanish term for Game Round. Preserve the unresolved timing distinction.

ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 52 expressly allows reactivating a Console previously activated by an opponent; EN p. 57 does not contain the corresponding sentence. One successful activation extracts one CivEvaced subject.

record.name: Hardlock
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Hardlock: Activate three centerline Consoles, pick up and Control the opposing Beacon, and complete one Classified Objective.

condition.text: At the end of each Game Round, be the only player with a non-Null Trooper as a Model (not a Marker) in Silhouette contact with the Enemy Beacon; enemy Troopers in contact prevent Control.
At the end of the game, your own Beacon is not Controlled by the enemy.
Complete your single Classified Objective (1 Objective Point).

rules.name: Deployment and objective positions
paragraphs: Sides A and B deploy on opposite table edges in game-size-specific Deployment Zones. Troopers may not deploy in Silhouette contact with any Beacon or Console.

There are two Beacons, one for each player, positioned in the middle of the front edge of each Deployment Zone. The one beside the opponent's Deployment Zone is the Enemy Beacon. Three Consoles stand along the table centerline: one at the center, with the others [[distance:6:inch]] from the side edges at 150 points, [[distance:8:inch]] at 200/250 points and [[distance:12:inch]] at 300/350/400 points. Each Console uses a Console A Token or scenery of the same diameter as that Token; the ITS 17 mission does not state an independent millimeter diameter.

rules.name: Pick Up Beacon

requirements: The player must have an Activated Console.
The Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with either a friendly Trooper in Normal State carrying the Enemy Beacon, or an unaccompanied Enemy Beacon without an opposing non-Null Trooper in contact.
effects: Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Enemy Beacon without making a Roll. Follow the Common Rules of Beacons.
sourceNotes: The Spanish source calls the prerequisite a Connected Console rather than an Activated Console; the wording remains an unresolved source discrepancy.

paragraphs: Pick Up Beacon is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill, requiring that the player has an Activated Console. The Trooper must also be in Silhouette contact either with a friendly Trooper in Normal State carrying the Enemy Beacon, or with an unaccompanied Enemy Beacon with no opposing non-Null Trooper in contact.

Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Enemy Beacon without a Roll. Follow the Common Rules of Beacons. The Spanish source calls the prerequisite a Connected Console rather than an Activated Console; see the source issue below.

rules.name: Common Rules of Beacons
paragraphs: Each Model can carry one Beacon; a Trooper with the Baggage Special Skill can carry up to two. Only Models, not Markers (including Camouflaged, Impersonation or Holoecho Markers), may carry a Beacon.

Beacons remain on the table and in Silhouette contact with their carrier. When the carrier enters or is in a Null State, the Beacon is dropped slightly outside Silhouette contact. Beacons do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Control an Enemy Beacon
paragraphs: A player Controls an Enemy Beacon only while that player alone has at least one Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Opposing Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Activate Console

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate the Console. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
A player may Activate a Console already Activated by the opponent, removing the previous player's Activated status. Different Player Tokens can track the current player.

paragraphs: Activate Console is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console must succeed on a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts can be repeated, spending a Short Skill for each attempt.

A player may Activate a Console already Activated by the opponent, using the same procedure. The previous player's Activated status is removed. Different Player Tokens can indicate which player currently has each Console Activated.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops in Hardlock.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Classified Objective
paragraphs: Each player has one Classified Objective, worth 1 Objective Point if completed.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 60 requires an Activated Console to Pick Up Beacon, whereas ES p. 55 says 'Consola Conectada'; its activation procedure on ES pp. 56-57 uses both Conectada and Activada. Preserve the terminology discrepancy without asserting a second Console state.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 60 requires a friendly Beacon carrier in Normal State for transfer; ES p. 55 does not repeat the Normal State qualification. Preserve the English restriction and the bilingual gap.
